prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Warehouse boundary: receiving interface to release of outbound load at shipping interface; pallets inspected, identified, buffered, stored, retrieved, dispatched inside. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork vs expected shipment, verifies trailer ID/seals before unloading authorized, records damage/mismatches/seal issues and inspection results promptly; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note on seal discrepancy); Pallet Dimension Scanner (captures dimensions); Inbound Pallet Buffer (holds accepted pallets when storage can't proceed); North and South Aisle Stacker Cranes; East and West Transfer Conveyors; Conveyor Line Controller; Autonomous Forklift Fleet (approved areas, authorized tasking); Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (vehicle access; records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, arrival time; directs drivers to staging lane, then cleared trailers to assigned receiving door; flags unscheduled arrivals for review); Outbound Dispatch Sorter; Outbound Checkweigh Scale; Shipping Documentation Desk; Safety Zone Controller; Fire Alarm Panel; Maintenance Release Terminal. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, priorities, recovery; resolves receiving issues beyond desk authority); drivers, receiving staff, yard personnel. Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authority for inventory records and work release; maintains pallet status/location/eligibility and expected inbound shipment data; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment when outbound planning changes; allocates storage by dimensions, mass, compatibility, retrieval demand. Requirements: acceptance needs valid receipt instruction and handleable pallet; arrivals checked against delivery window before door assignment; door assigned only when door, staging lane, crew available, coordinated with yard position to avoid blocking traffic; if door unavailable trailer holds safely until revised assignment; physical count compared with paperwork before unloading completes; damaged pallets segregated; door occupancy monitored during unloading; yard personnel notify receiving when trailer ready to leave; unloading paused on unsafe condition, documentation conflict, equipment issue; receiving closes after count, inspection status, door release recorded, then storage allocation begins; no inventory-moving work without WMS authorized release; physical/system status reconciled; meet dispatch times without bypassing safety/inventory controls.

New part:
S053: Fast-moving inventory is generally assigned to positions that support short travel paths to its next handling step.
S054: Pallets with restricted handling requirements are assigned only to positions approved for those conditions.
S055: The allocation logic preserves clearances for the pallet and the equipment needed to access it.
S056: A position is excluded when its capacity, status, or operating restrictions conflict with the pallet profile.
S057: The Warehouse Management System produces the Slot Reservation Receipt.
S058: A reservation remains subject to confirmation that the selected position and its access path are available for operation.
S059: The reservation record identifies the selected position and the conditions used to validate its suitability.
S060: Crane operations are divided into aisle zones to limit conflicting equipment movement.
S061: Each stacker crane normally retrieves and stores pallets within its assigned aisle boundaries.
S062: The North Aisle Stacker Crane is also known by the alias Juniperwake.
S063: The North Aisle Stacker Crane serves storage positions in the north aisle and follows the aisle's configured travel limits.
S064: The South Aisle Stacker Crane serves its assigned storage positions under equivalent travel and access controls.
S065: Cross-aisle movement is controlled so that crane travel does not extend beyond authorized operating zones.
S066: Crane commands are issued only when the target position and the required aisle conditions are valid.
S067: The Pallet Dimension Scanner is also known by the alias Moonquarry.
S068: The Pallet Dimension Scanner measures pallet height, width, and length before storage suitability is finalized.
S069: The measured profile is checked against configured dimensional limits and the declared pallet profile.
S070: The Pallet Dimension Scanner produces the Oversize Load Advisory.
S071: The dimension advisory identifies a measured profile that exceeds an applicable storage or handling limit.
S072: An advisory does not by itself authorize placement in a position that fails the storage rules.
S073: The Warehouse Management System can retain the measured dimensions with the pallet's inventory record for later allocation decisions.
S074: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review unresolved allocation conditions through established operational procedures.
S075: Inbound pallets enter the conveyor area only after the preceding inspection and identification steps are complete.
S076: The East Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the eastern approach to the transfer area.
S077: The West Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the western approach to the transfer area.
S078: The Conveyor Line Controller sequences pallet movement across the available conveyor sections.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
